newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oerlikon rules out Bally spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Oerlikon rules out Bally spin-off.

text.p: Shoes-to-guns maker Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG said a public offering for shoes and fashion division Bally, which has been speculated about in Swiss media, would not make sense.
Oerlikon Chairman Hans Widmer said in a statement the group was willing to find money for extensive restructuring at Bally from other sources than a spin-off.

Widmer said Bally head Ernmst Thomke had started the speculation by telling journalists in May he needed more money to complete a major reorganisation of the shoemaker and retailer, including remodeling its shops around the world.
"One theoretical possibility for doing this is going public and offering part of the Bally shares to the public," Widmer said.
Widmer said the group's policy on its mixed portfolio of five divisions was to offer stakes to outsiders if this was necessary for a division's development and also benefited Oerlikon shareholders.
"The chairman of Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding believes the concrete conditions are not appropriate for going public (with Bally)," Widmer said.
"The chairman is prepared to provide the funds for worthwhile projects at Bally from other sources," the statement added without elaborating.

Swiss newspapers have speculated for days that Thomke, who was brought in 20 months ago to revive loss-making Bally, was locked in a power struggle with major shareholder and board member Horstense Anda-Buerhle over whether to offer Bally shares.
Thomke was reported to be pushing for a spin-off with Oerlikon retaining majority ownership while Anda-Buehrle, heiress of the Buehrle family, wanted to keep the group in its current shape.
Widmer did not comment directly on the media reports.
But Widmer confirmed that Thomke would give the board of directors a presentation on August 18 of his proposal to speed up Bally's restructuring with a cash infusion.
Widmer said the added money would be "primarily for additional marketing and a more rapid concentration in shop locations that correspond to the needs of a world-wide brand".
Thomke had first made the proposal at a board meeting on may 21 and was asked to return with a detailed presentation in August, Widmer said.
